newsitem.title: USA: GM won't comment on Hughes bid reports.
newsitem.headline: GM won't comment on Hughes bid reports.

text.p: General Motors Corp declined to comment Monday on reports that Raytheon Co has gained an edge over Northrop Grumman Corp in the bidding for GM's Hughes Electronics Corp defense operations.
A GM spokeswoman declined to comment on the bidding process, or whether GM planned any special board meetings this week. Raytheon and Northrop spokesmen earlier declined comment.
GM Chairman Jack Smith on Sunday said the board had no plans to meet Monday or Tuesday. He added that GM is "just trying to get top dollar" for the Hughes assets.
However, a source close to the situation said GM's board could meet via teleconference to consider and approve such divestitures or acquisitions.

The source also said a speech by Hughes Chairman C. Michael Armstrong to the Economic Club of Detroit scheduled for Wednesday was not intended to announce or discuss a sale of the assets and does not mean a deal is imminent.
The speech "was agreed to before all this speculation," the source said.
In his speech, Armstrong will discuss international trade issues and his role as the chairman of President Bill Clinton's Export Council. Smith also will appear at the luncheon.
Armstrong is scheduled to hold a news conference at 1030 EST/1530 GMT on Wednesday, but such media availability is customary for speakers to the Detroit business group.
